tasks.how: Frequency: Weekly (Mon).; In Talkwalker, rank brands by SOV growth over the last 30 days, from highest to lowest. Keep the top 8 to 10 brands (ideally 10).
tasks.check: 8 to 10 brands listed, ordered by growth.

tasks.how: Frequency: Weekly.; Click the brand, set the 30-day window, sort by top engagement and read 100 to 200 posts manually. Note each irrelevant post and why it was collected.
tasks.check: 100 to 200 posts read; noise noted with cause and link.

tasks.how: Frequency: Weekly.; Sort results by random and read 100 to 200 posts manually. Note noise and its cause.
tasks.check: 100 to 200 posts read; noise noted with cause and link.

tasks.how: Frequency: Weekly.; On the brand: Widget action menu > Export all results > CSV > Random sample > choose the number of results (thousands) > Select a custom export format: Simplified export > Export all results. CSV is lighter and easier to analyse with AI.
tasks.check: CSV downloaded with the right period and sample size.

tasks.how: Frequency: Weekly.; Upload the CSV to the AI assistant with a prompt asking it to detect noise unrelated to the brand, giving the brand's query keywords as context. Ask for noise grouped by cause, with examples and proposed exclusion terms.
tasks.tools: AI assistant, CSV export, brand query
tasks.check: Each noise group validated against real posts.

tasks.how: Frequency: Weekly.; When a post has no link at all with the brand, it can be deleted from the results in Talkwalker. Only delete posts that are unambiguously off-topic; otherwise use an exclusion.
tasks.check: Every deleted post double-checked as fully unrelated to the brand.

tasks.how: Frequency: Weekly.; On the 100 to 200 posts reviewed, check that sentiment matches the post (positive, negative, neutral) and correct it directly in Talkwalker. Priority: top engagement posts, so what the client sees and the dashboard are right.
tasks.check: Top engagement posts carry the right sentiment.

tasks.how: Frequency: Weekly.; Open the Consumer voice filter and check for noise. Note irrelevant posts and terms.
tasks.check: Noise noted with cause.

tasks.how: Frequency: Weekly.; Select categories together or at random (skincare, makeup, fragrance; face, eyes, lips, body) and check matched posts. Note what is relevant and what is noise.
tasks.check: Each segment checked at least on a sample.

tasks.how: Frequency: Weekly.; Check the Luxury drivers filters for noise: Social & environmental engagement, Health & well-being benefits, Global product excellence, Uniqueness & style, Strong emotion, Experience & co-creation.
tasks.check: Each driver checked on a sample.

tasks.task: Apply exclusions & fix the brand query
tasks.how: Frequency: Weekly.; Combine the noise terms from phases 1 and 3 into NOT exclusions, test them following Phase 8 (query writing rules), then update the brand query / filters.
tasks.check: Exclusion tested in preview; no visible loss of relevant posts.

tasks.how: Frequency: Weekly.; For each brand, fill the weekly cleaning sheet: status, issue found, action taken, link examples.
tasks.check: One block per brand, all four checks filled.

tasks.task: Rank queries by number of wildcards
tasks.how: Frequency: On client request.; List brands and custom filters by number of wildcards (*) and start with the heaviest ones.
tasks.check: Every brand / filter has a wildcard count and a status (Checked / To be checked).

tasks.how: Frequency: On client request.; In each query, use Ctrl+F / Cmd+F to find every *. For each one, decide which explicit words it should cover (e.g. gift* > gift OR gifts OR gifting OR gifted) and rewrite. See sheet 'Wildcard examples'. Goal: a lighter topic so the analytics dashboard is not too heavy.
tasks.check: Each replacement covers the forms consumers actually use; no new noise.

tasks.how: Frequency: On client request.; Record mentions before and after the rewrite (count, difference, % change) and compare the topic volume on the same period.
tasks.check: Volume stable or explained (e.g. Skincare 31.7K > 31.4K).

tasks.how: Frequency: When needed.; Click each brand, set a period of 3 months or 1 year. Manually check 100 to 150 posts in top engagement and 100 to 150 in random, per luxury driver.
tasks.check: Each driver reviewed on both views.
tasks.output: Relevance notes per brand x driver

tasks.how: Frequency: When needed.; Export about 1,000 posts (CSV) and run an AI classification of relevant / not relevant per driver; check the output post by post.
tasks.check: AI classification spot-checked.
tasks.output: Relevance estimate per driver + fixes to propose

tasks.how: Frequency: Each query change.; Copy the query, open a new topic and click Preview query (max 1 month). Check the volume, then the 25 posts shown, in top engagement and in random.
tasks.check: Volume plausible; the 25 posts look relevant in both views.

tasks.task: Write exclusions below the main query
tasks.how: Frequency: Each query change.; Write the noise exclusions in the exclusion block below the main query. Before saving, check that no exclusion term can also appear in relevant brand posts.
tasks.check: No exclusion likely to remove relevant volume.

tasks.task: Add a new franchise from the client request
tasks.how: Frequency: Per client request.; Start from the client's request for a new franchise (e.g. [brand] [franchise]) and add it to the franchise list to be tagged.
tasks.check: Franchise name and brand confirmed with the client request.

tasks.how: Frequency: Per franchise request.; Create a dedicated tag for the franchise.
tasks.check: Tag name follows the existing naming convention.

tasks.how: Frequency: Per franchise request.; In Settings, create a rule that applies the tag to future mentions, and apply it to past data. Scope the rule to the right topics only, never to all topics.
tasks.check: Rule scoped to the right topics; tag visible on past data once processed.

tasks.task: Add the franchise to the filter
tasks.how: Frequency: Per franchise request.; Write the query for the specific franchise. Be careful if the franchise name is too generic.
tasks.check: Query tested with Preview query or quick search.

tasks.how: Frequency: When needed.; Open the rule in Settings, correct the query or filter, then re-apply the rule to past data so the correction covers the history. Avoid running many corrections at the same time.
tasks.check: Rule re-applied to past data after the change.

tasks.how: Frequency: Urgent only.; When the client needs data immediately, tag the existing results manually instead of waiting for the rule.
tasks.check: Existing results tagged; rule still created for future mentions.

tasks.how: Frequency: Per franchise request.; Check the new franchise appears in the campaign tracking dashboard. For fragrance categories, integration is automatic once the brand is filled in.
tasks.check: Franchise visible and comparable with other franchises.
